svg.title: 11 skills, one line each — why having them all costs almost nothing
svg.desc: An animated diagram of the kit's 11 Bob skills. The six main-chain skills and the three situational ones appear in turn as cards, each showing its one-line description and what its body would cost. A readout counts up to roughly 755 tokens: that is the entire standing cost of the descriptions. A stacked bar then shows what you actually pay in the context window — Bob's own baseline of about 9,230 tokens plus that sliver — and a second bar shows the counterfactual: if all 11 skill bodies were always loaded it would cost about 10,933 tokens instead, roughly 14 times as much, every single turn, spent on instructions you are not using.
svg.text: Only the description sits in context. The body loads on demand.
THE MAIN CHAIN — the six stages, in order
WHEN THEY APPLY — and only then

g.text: Gather verified real-world evidence about a
product or service idea before designing it.
Interview the team relentlessly about their plan
until there is one shared understanding,
recording settled vocabulary in GLOSSARY.md and
Turn a settled design conversation into a written
Build a feature test-first and carry it to the
Design an evaluation set and grader for the AI
part of the product, then improve against it one
Harden a project for a live demo in front of an
audience and rehearse the failure modes.
What that actually costs, in the context window
Tokens are characters ÷ 4. Both bars are a few percent of Bob’s 270,000-token window — but you pay them on every single turn.
